Subject: Resale certificate required to process volume rebate / invoice #INV-9042

Hi Dana / Maple Retail billing team,

Quick note — we have placed invoice INV-9042 (June usage) on hold for application of the volume rebate you negotiated with our Sales team. Before we can finalize the credit, finance needs a valid resale exemption certificate on file covering the billing address and states listed on the invoice (primarily CA).

What we need from you:
- A signed resale certificate for California (CDTFA-230 or equivalent state form).
- The seller name and seller registration (if any) present on the form.
- Effective date and whether this is a blanket/reseller certificate or transaction-specific (blanket preferred).

I attached a short example (required_cert_example.pdf) to show the fields our tax team validates. If you can upload the signed certificate to the HubSpot record (link below) or reply to this thread with the PDF, we’ll validate and apply the rebate.

If we receive the certificate by end of next business day we can target applying the credit to the next billing cycle; otherwise the credit will be applied after validation on the following cycle.

Thanks — let me know if the form needs to route to someone else.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Billing & Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Dana — blanket CA resale certificate is fine. Two things finance will check when validating:

1) Seller name MUST match the bill-to name on the invoice (Maple Retail LLC).
2) The certificate needs to indicate it is effective for the period during which the sales occurred (covering June 2026).

Optional but helpful: seller registration number (state-issued), buyer’s use description, and a physical address match. If you include EIN it helps our records but isn’t required for CA validation.

We can provisionally release the hold and apply a provisional credit if we receive the signed certificate by end of day Monday. If the certificate fails validation later we’ll contact you immediately — we rarely see issues but want to be transparent.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
